newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says will donate 40,000 T of rice to Africa.
newsitem.headline: Japan says will donate 40,000 T of rice to Africa.

text.p: The Japanese government decided on Friday to donate about 40,000 tonnes of rice to eight African countries, officials said.

Agriculture Ministry officials said the government would give a total of about 1.9 billion yen to eight African countries -- Angola, Ghana, Cape Verde, Burkina Faso, Guinea, Comoros, Rwanda and Djibouti -- to buy about 40,000 tonnes of rice from Japan, making it effectively a rice donation.

Last November, the Japanese government decided to send nearly 60,000 tonnes of rice to poor countries in Africa, Asia and Central America but this has not yet been shipped. The new supplies for Africa would increase the total to 100,000 tonnes.
We're going to hold negotiations with the eight countries on allocating the rice," a ministry official said.
Shipment of the crop have not yet been decided, the officials said.
Local grain traders said the rice aid is an attempt to reduce swollen rice stocks here. Good harvests in the past two years have swollen stocks in grain warehouses in Japan.

The Agriculture Ministry has estimated that domestic rice stocks at the end of last October stood at three million tonnes. A stock level of 1.5 million tonnes is considered desirable throughout the year.
Rice exporters, such as Australia, have expressed concern that any offshore rice donations of foreign rice imported under Japan's GATT obligations would go against the spirit of the trade agreement.
Under the 1993 GATT Uruguay Round agreements, Japan agreed to gradually open its long-closed rice market and committed itself to importing a specific quantity of rice per year.
Japan has not said whether foreign rice will be included in its donations.
One Agriculture Ministry official said it was not clear at this stage whether foreign rice will be shipped to the African countries as aid.
